notes.note: Reading 1 chosen: relevant = referenced in the alternatives. The test blocks on a disconnected port holding a non-matching message, a never-started timer and a stopped (not killed) alive PTC; expects a dynamic error.
Literal reading chosen; checks that an active default matching the queued message is not entered when the alt has an else branch.
Reading 1 chosen: the optional block runs after a selected altstep alternative.
Restriction reading chosen: goto in an altstep branch cannot leave the calling alt; this overlaps with the goto scope rules of 19.6 (Titan reports an undefined label).
Titan accepts: it does not check side effects of functions called in guards (component variable change). Test is correct per 20.2 b) / 16.1.4 g).
Titan accepts: it does not check that functions called in guards are free of setverdict (16.1.4 h)).
Titan accepts: it does not check side effects of functions called in the event's matching part (16.1.4 g)).
Titan accepts: it does not check that a function called in a receive template performs no port operation (16.1.4 b)).
The side effect comes from an altstep local definition initialised with a function that changes a component variable (16.1.5/16.1.4 g)); Titan does not check this.
Titan accepts: it does not check side effects in actual parameters of altsteps invoked as alternatives.
Reading 1 chosen. A non-timeout event in a control-part alt is also forbidden by the general ban on component and port operations in control, so the test cannot isolate this rule.
"call statements" is taken as the response and exception handling part of blocking calls; the test uses repeat directly in a testcase body.
Reading 1 chosen; the test covers the altstep-call case only. Titan does not reject activate inside interleave, so that variant was not used.
A non-timeout event in control is also forbidden by the general ban on component and port operations in control, so the test cannot isolate this rule.

Titan rejects: it forbids goto/label anywhere inside interleave, which deviates from 20.4 restriction d). The goto stays in a statement block without reception statements, so the test is correct per the standard.
Titan accepts: it does not implement the restriction on loops containing reception statements inside interleave.
Reading 1 chosen: both the goto and its label are in one block without reception statements. Titan rejects goto/label in interleave entirely, which deviates from 20.4 d).
Titan rejects goto in interleave entirely, although 20.4 d) explicitly allows jumps out of interleave statements.
